item.title: Roger Cook chides Labor MPs after fracas at parliament door
item.description: WA Premier Roger Cook reminds MPs of their responsibilities after a group of Labor members tried to shield their colleague Jags Krishnan from media questioning as he entered parliament yesterday. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after a final count on Wednesday, becoming the state's first Black US senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory adds to the Democrats' midterm gains as President Donald Trump's party suffers a series of defeats. Publicado también por: France 24 - English, Al Jazeera English. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: U.S. midterm election results 2026: List of key winners
item.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 states went for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Netanyahu asks military to prepare for Iran 2.0; opp says no strikes before next gov
item.description: Amid rising tensions, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet has initiated military preparations for a possible strike on Iran. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot advocates for careful judgment from the caretaker administration during this transitional period, emphasizing that military actions should only be executed in the face of direct threats to Israel. He highlights concerns about Netanyahu's decreasing support in the Knesset, which currently stands at just 46 votes. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Marrickville Golf Club says Anthony Albanese's membership worth $1,100

item.title: Los demócratas agrandan su victoria histórica en las ‘midterms’: también se imponen en Misisipi
item.description: ﻿Las ‘midterms’ tienen todavía más peso histórico desde este miércoles: tras un recuento de infarto, se ha confirmado la victoria del candidato demócrata, Scott Colom, al escaño de senador por Misisipi, un territorio dominado durante décadas por los republicanos.Después de más de una semana de recuento, Colom aventajaba en casi cinco mil votos a su rival republicana, Cindy Hyde-Smith, ya sin margen en el escrutinio para recuperar la distancia. La republicana reconoció su derrota y puso fin a la espera. «No es el resultado por el que trabajamos y el que esperábamos, pero respeto la decisión de… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

item.description: La victoria de Colom lo convierte además en el primer senador demócrata en Misisipi desde 1982. Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: Directo a... Asunción y los hasta 15 años de cárcel a los que se podría enfrentar expresidente Peña
item.description: El Ministerio Público de Paraguay expuso el marco penal por el que está siendo investigado el depuesto presidente, Santiago Peña, quien podría enfrentarse hasta 15 años de cárcel por presunta lesión de confianza y administración en beneficio propio. Nuestra corresponsal Flavia Borja nos amplió la información sobre los avances de la investigación contra el exmandatario y la solicitud de apoyo internacional para rastrear el dinero perdido de Ueno Bank, la entidad cuyo cierre derivó en la destitución de Peña. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: US midterms: Democrat Colom defeats Hyde-Smith in Mississippi to win historic Senate seat
item.description: Democratic challenger Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi election for the US Senate, media projected on Wednesday, making him the Southern state’s first black senator since the Reconstruction era that followed the US Civil War. The result was a stunning upset in the ‌heavily Republican state and expanded on the national drubbing the Democrats delivered to President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections. The Mississippi victory... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Can Southeast Asia cut and paste Australia’s AI safeguards?
item.description: Australia’s new mandatory safeguards on AI companies could serve as a model for Southeast Asia, analysts say, but the region needs to build its institutional and technical capabilities first. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on Tuesday that AI companies operating in Australia must immediately report incidents in which their models behave in a rogue or misaligned way and must open systems for evaluation. The measures followed a breach of Australia’s government health data system in June... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: ¿Misión de rescate o apuesta política de Bukele?: dudas por el despliegue militar de El Salvador en Haití
item.description: A finales de octubre, el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, anunció el envío de militares de su país para rescatar a cuatro técnicos de aviación salvadoreños, desaparecidos el 18 de octubre durante una emboscada de pandilleros en Puerto Príncipe. El opaco despliegue de 2.000 soldados, sin coordinación internacional aunque con el acuerdo del Gobierno haitiano, ha despertado interrogantes sobre el objetivo de la misión, su contribución real en un contexto convulso y su cumplimiento del derecho internacional. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: UK appoints world’s first special representative for climate security
item.description: Exclusive: Madeleine Alessandri, chair of the joint intelligence committee, will take on the role of advising No 10 on climate-related national security risks The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country. Prime minister Andy Burnham will announce the move on Thursday at Cop31, the UN climate summit, with the new role designed to advise the government on national security risks from the climate crisis before they spell catastrophe. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: León XIV ya está en Perú, su segunda patria, por primera vez desde su elección como papa
item.description: Fue recibido por la presidenta Keiko Fujimori. Tras más de dos décadas como misionero y obispo en el país, el pontífice concluye su gira sudamericana en la tierra a la que atribuye haberle enseñado a ser pastor. Durante su estadía, oficiará celebraciones religiosas en Chiclayo, la Amazonía y Cusco, donde abordará diversas problemáticas sociales y ambientales. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot unveils agenda to reverse Netanyahu’s policies
item.description: The bloc of Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot introduced a series of bills at the start of the legislative session that target Benjamin Netanyahu and his policies. They include launching an official government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks, setting term limits on the position of prime minister and overturning changes the outgoing Netanyahu-led government made to limit the powers of the judiciary. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Rina Bassist, Editor at Al-Monitor. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Sharon GAFFNEY

item.title: General strike over housing brings out hundreds of thousands in Spain
item.description: Millions of workers in Spain shut down businesses and public transport on Wednesday, as part of the country's first general strike in 14 years. Following a peaceful march in Barcelona over soaring rents and property prices, and the rising cost of living, protesters smashed storefronts, set off small bonfires, burned bins and launched fireworks towards police. The unrest comes just weeks before snap elections, called by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Low-hanging fruit for Xi and Trump to pluck at Shenzhen Apec summit
item.description: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is set to take place in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. Shenzhen will also be playing host to the first of two further meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump this year. When the two leaders met in May and September, they called for “constructive strategic stability” as a prescription for US-China relations. Both sides are keen to maintain the fragile detente, in part due to domestic considerations. Beijing wants to... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: El 'ministerio del Noviazgo' en Brasil: Lula y su promesa de que todo el mundo va a tener pareja
item.description: “En mi Gobierno, todo el mundo va a tener pareja”. Esta fue la promesa que Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva hizo a los brasileños durante la campaña electoral de 2022, cuando aspiraba a conquistar su tercer mandato. Ahora, sus seguidores intentan materializar esa iniciativa. En la misma línea, el papa, en su gira por Suramérica, clamó: "Atrévanse a dar el paso casándose y formando una familia. ¡No le teman al para siempre!". ¿Qué tan grave es el problema de la soledad? Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Biden says he wouldn’t have run for second term if he’d known he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he did not know he had cancer while he was US president and would not have sought a second term if he already had been diagnosed. The former Democratic president’s comments came in an interview with People magazine before the release of his White House memoir on Tuesday. “If I had known that I was feeling lousy because I had cancer,” said Biden, who turns 84 on November 20, “I would’ve not gone forward” with a 2024 re-election bid that ended after a disastrous debate performance... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: US President Donald Trump used a Veterans Day commemoration on Wednesday to defend the war against Iran – an increasingly unpopular conflict that helped trigger a Democratic takeover of Congress in last week’s midterm elections. “The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington. “When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better... But he can’t claim they represent a fresh expression of confidence. The project has been on the runway since the German utility RWE, the developer, was awarded a contract to build… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: 13 mil reproducciones · 292 reacciones | #Eleição2026 - O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) decidiu nesta terça-feira (10), por unanimidade, multar em R$ 7,5 milhões a empresa Meta (dona do Facebook, WhatsApp e Instagram) por descumprimento de decisões da Corte durante as eleições. Os ministros seguiram o voto do relator, ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, para aplicar a punição à empresa Meta por deixar de cumprir integralmente determinações da Corte para garantir isonomia na disputal presidencial, substituindo prazos judiciais fixados pelo TSE por prazos próprios, além de falta de transparência. Além disso, afirma que a empresa apresentou informações de forma fracionada ao tribunal, em linguagem estrangeira e técnica, o que dificultou a verificação de dificuldades técnicas apontadas para justificar falhas. Os ministros analisaram uma ação da campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que foi reeleito, e aponta que houve um tratamento desigual na distribuição de conteúdos políticos e na veiculação de anúncios eleitorais durante o segundo turno das eleições. Segundo Bellizze, "as plataformas digitais exercem poder informacional que condiciona, por sistemas algorítmicos pouco transparentes, a circulação da informação política e a formação da vontade do eleitor". O ministro afirmou que as regras do TSE impõem aos provedores deveres voltados à proteção da integridade do processo eleitoral, que decorrem de sua função social e de seu dever de cuidado. Com isso, considera que a imposição de multa e de outras medidas necessárias é indispensável para assegurar o cumprimento das decisões desta Justiça especializada. item.title: Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, the politician tasked with forming a new Israeli government, pledged on Tuesday to launch an official inquiry into Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks and reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies as the new parliament was sworn in a tense opening session that saw rival parties trade barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists. Fuente: France 24 - English.
